images.caption: Misgeach Power Station. Small hydroelectric station making use of compensation water discharged into the Uisge Misgeach from the Lochiel tunnel from Loch Monar, which crosses the valley in an inverted syphon.  This spectacular discharge means the station is NOT running!  It rarely does operate.

images.caption: Hydro Electric Shaft The large vertical shaft is an air vent for the N.O.S.H.E.B (North of Scotland Hydro Electric Board) underground pipe line, from Loch Beinn a' Mheadhoin (Loch Benevean), to the Fasnakyle Power Station. The turbines first powered up and generated electricity to the National Grid, on 19th July 1951. The water can be heard thundering through the tunnel.
images.alt: Hydro Electric Shaft The large vertical shaft is an air vent for the N.O.S.H.E.B (North of Scotland Hydro Electric Board) underground pipe line, from Loch Beinn a' Mheadhoin (Loch Benevean), to the Fasnakyle Power Station. The turbines first powered up and generated electricity to the National Grid, on 19th July 1951. The water can be heard thundering through the tunnel.

images.caption: Tunnel entrance The tunnel is for inspecting the Hydro-electric underground water pipe line, from the dam at Loch Beinn a' Mheadhoin (Loch Benevean), to Fasnakyle Power Station. The turbines were switched on for the first time on 19th July 1951. The overgrown entrance, suggests that the gates have obviously not been opened for many years.
images.alt: Tunnel entrance The tunnel is for inspecting the Hydro-electric underground water pipe line, from the dam at Loch Beinn a' Mheadhoin (Loch Benevean), to Fasnakyle Power Station. The turbines were switched on for the first time on 19th July 1951. The overgrown entrance, suggests that the gates have obviously not been opened for many years.
